chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah al-Hashimi, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): Is it permissible for the owner of wealth, when he wishes to secure his own capital, to make a portion of it a partnership so that it becomes more secure for him in his wealth? He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use partnership structures to secure investment capital in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) permits an investor to designate a portion of his capital as a partnership (*shirka*) to serve as collateral (*ithaq*), thereby enhancing security for his assets. This ruling highlights the flexibility of Shia commercial jurisprudence in allowing hybrid financial structures where partnership serves not only for profit-sharing but also as a risk-mitigation tool. It underscores the principle that contractual arrangements in Islam are adaptable to practical economic needs while remaining within the bounds of Shariah.
